sentence: Most children diagnosed with HL are cured with first-line therapy options and have an excellent prognosis; the 5-year survival rate for early stage disease exceeds 90% ref [216].

For those individuals in whom initial therapy fails, several novel therapeutic approaches are available, including stem cell transplant, the use of monoclonal antibodies, chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy, and immunotherapy ref [129].
An estimated 40% of patients in whom traditional chemotherapy and radiation treatment regimens fail respond to these second-line therapies ref [129].
This risk remains elevated even decades after treatment ref [213].
For this reason, most childhood HL survivors require lifelong surveillance and cancer risk reduction strategies ref [213].

However, as therapies continue to evolve and become more narrowly tailored in pediatric populations, it is likely that the rates of organ toxicities, late mortality, and secondary malignancies will continue to decline ref [214].
Long-term survivors of HL are at high risk of various organ toxicities secondary to their therapeutic regimens ref [48].
